Project overview

  • Team: Cross-functional fintech delivery squad (Lead UX Designer, Product Managers, Frontend Engineers, Regulatory Compliance Officers, Data Analysts)
  • Core skills demonstrated: Complex Data Visualisation, Design Systems, Regulatory & Accessibility Compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA), CRO Architecture, Cross-functional Stakeholder Management

What this project proves about me: I excel at translating dense, strictly regulated financial information into clear, human-centred digital experiences that systematically drive commercial conversion and product engagement.

The challenge

Consumer credit data is notoriously complex, intimidating, and emotionally charged. The existing myEquifax digital touchpoints suffered from severe structural friction:

  1. High cognitive load and jargon: Credit files were presented as dense, bureaucratic walls of text. Users struggled to parse why their score changed or which accounts contributed to fluctuations.
  2. Low habitual engagement: The platform was treated as a transactional, single-use utility—users checked their score once during major life events (e.g., applying for a mortgage) and rarely returned.
  3. Commercial misalignment: The product marketplace felt disconnected and intrusive. Promoted credit cards and loans appeared as generic advertisements rather than tailored solutions, dampening user trust and conversion rates (CvR).
  4. Strict compliance constraints: Every data display, notification, and recommendation was governed by rigid financial compliance standards, meaning UX improvements had to preserve statutory audit trails and legal transparency without adding interface clutter.

My process

To manage this multi-surface overhaul within an enterprise fintech environment, I used a structured, iterative framework:

  1. Quantitative & Qualitative Discovery: Evaluated user session drop-offs and navigation bottlenecks using Adobe Analytics, user session replays, and support ticket trends.
  2. Information Architecture & Wireframing: Deconstructed credit reports into modular, card-based information hierarchies, running quick unmoderated tree tests to validate categorization.
  3. Component Systematisation: Built a tokenised design system in Figma to unify typography, data-point visualisations, and interactive states between iOS, Android, and responsive web.
  4. Regulatory & Technical Feasibility Alignment: Partnered with compliance officers and frontend engineers early in sprint cycles to validate data disclosure boundaries and API limitations.
  5. Iterative Prototyping & Usability Testing: Tested high-fidelity prototypes across core cohorts to evaluate icon comprehension, report legibility, and sharing permission comfort levels.
  6. Staged Implementation & CRO Experimentation: Rolled out redesigned modules systematically, measuring task completion times and commercial click-through rates against legacy baselines.

What I did

1. Product Iconography & Visual Systems

Figure 1: The high-fidelity responsive application interface featuring the central credit score dial, historical trend lines, and contextual categories.

Financial terminology often disorients users. I engineered a purpose-built iconography system to anchor core feature navigation. By replacing generic generic UI symbols with colour-coded, conceptually distinct icons, I established clear visual hierarchy throughout the application shell.

Figure 2: Dedicated product icon suite developed for Equifax consumer touchpoints, balancing brand identity with functional clarity.

I validated visual comprehension through targeted usability testing before pushing tokens to engineering. This reduced ambiguity across navigation menus, cutting down accidental taps and boosting first-touch navigation velocity.

2. Credit Report Redesign

Traditional credit disclosures read like legal summaries. I broke down this monolithic data structure into modular, consumable visual cards.

Figure 3: Side-by-side comparative analysis annotating specific UX enhancements between the legacy reporting screens and the updated modular structure.

Key interventions included:

  • Replacing raw numerical tables with interactive trend graphs and status-coded pill badges.
  • Removing excessive whitespace while adopting an accessible, mobile-first typographic scale compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA standards.
  • Collaborating with Legal & Compliance teams to introduce progressive disclosure patterns, ensuring regulatory disclosures remained fully accessible without overwhelming primary scan paths.

3. Family & Friends Sharing

Financial literacy and collective household budgeting are major drivers of consumer loyalty. I led the UX architecture for the 'Family & Friends Plan', an initiative allowing primary account holders to securely share monitored insights with trusted contacts.

Figure 4: High-fidelity onboarding cards and account management interfaces for the multi-user Family & Friends permission system.

Because financial privacy is paramount, I engineered a multi-state permission model. The interface made privacy boundaries explicitly evident: users could view progress and high-level milestones without exposing sensitive personal identifiers, bank account numbers, or discrete debt balances.

4. Personalised Financial Marketplace

To increase secondary revenue without degrading consumer trust, I reimagined the product recommendation engine into an advisory marketplace.

Figure 5: Responsive marketplace view detailing targeted credit card and loan recommendations filtered by user eligibility.

Rather than presenting uncalibrated product carousels, I structured recommendations around eligibility indicators. Cards clearly highlighted why an offer matched the consumer's current credit standing, transforming banner-style adverts into personalized financial guidance and increasing qualified partner referrals.

5. Finance Monitor & Component Systems

To move myEquifax from passive review to active financial management, I designed 'Finance Monitor'—a proactive hub featuring real-time account tracking, notifications, and tailored improvement actions.

Figure 6: Responsive Finance Monitor overview displaying aggregated spending insights and connected banking data structures.

Figure 7: Component repository showing transaction rows, data visualisations, state dialogs, and reusable cards built for engineering handover.

I built a fully reusable component library in Figma, complete with defined auto-layout properties, responsive constraints, dark/light accessibility contrasts, and interactive states. This library aligned design specifications directly with React frontend components, cutting front-end implementation overhead.

Why I made these decisions

  1. Progressive Disclosure over Monolithic Data Dumps: Financial reports contain hundreds of attributes. By defaulting to high-level category summaries (e.g., Payment History, Credit Utilisation) and allowing users to expand detailed tradelines on demand, we protected casual users from cognitive overload while preserving exhaustive depth for power users.
  2. Contextualised Marketplace Placement: Placing credit offers inside educational context—such as suggesting balance transfer cards directly beside high-utilisation warnings—grounded commercial recommendations in genuine user utility rather than commercial interruption.
  3. Strict Visual Systematisation: Fintech applications cannot afford visual ambiguity. Unifying component paddings, iconography, and typography across platforms lowered frontend regression rates and built visual trust with security-conscious users.
  4. Opt-in Privacy Paradigms: In the Family & Friends feature, defaulting all data sharing permissions to 'Restricted' until explicitly toggled built immediate trust and navigated stringent UK financial privacy regulations without legal pushback.

Figure 8: Responsive design mock-up of the modernised myEquifax credit dashboard across desktop, laptop, and mobile devices, highlighting score tiering and historic performance tracking.

Impact / results

Objective / Focus Area UX & Commercial Outcome
User Engagement Restructured navigation and modular credit overviews streamlined key user journeys, leading to higher task completion rates and increased daily active sessions.
Conversion & CRO Aligning financial marketplace suggestions with personal credit eligibility produced measurable lifts in qualified application click-through rates.
User Retention Actionable proactive alerts in Finance Monitor transformed the app from an occasional audit tool into an ongoing financial health dashboard, lifting repeat monthly engagement.
Design Scalability Standardised UI components and comprehensive token handoffs noticeably accelerated sprint turnaround times between design sign-off and engineering delivery.

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / Skills Used
Design & Prototyping Figma, Design Systems Architecture, Responsive UI Design, Vector Iconography
Research & Validation Qualitative Usability Testing, Cognitive Walkthroughs, Information Architecture, Wireframing
Analytics & CRO Funnel Analysis, Adobe Analytics, Usability Heuristics, Conversion Rate Optimisation (CRO)
Technical & Governance WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility, React Component Handover, Fintech Compliance Integration, Jira

Roles performed on this project

  • Product UX Designer: End-to-end user journeys, high-fidelity UI design, and information architecture across mobile and web.
  • Design System Specialist: Built, documented, and governed scalable UI component libraries and custom iconography sets.
  • CRO Specialist: Structured marketplace flows and call-to-action hierarchies to maximise qualified lead generation.
  • Cross-Functional Partner: Coordinated directly with Product Managers, Compliance teams, and Frontend Developers to guarantee feasible, compliant implementation.

childMarkdownRemark.html: myEquifax is a flagship consumer financial health platform providing millions of users direct access to their credit scores, report monitoring, and financial products. However, dense technical reporting and legacy layouts created high cognitive fatigue, obscuring valuable tools and hindering commercial marketplace conversions. Operating as the Product UX Designer across a multi-year tenure, I led the core experience redesign across critical flows—including the credit dashboard, reporting hierarchy, permission-based sharing, and a targeted financial marketplace. By establishing a scalable design system, simplifying complex data visualisations, and collaborating directly with compliance and engineering teams, I transformed an intimidating credit archive into an actionable financial hub that elevated daily engagement, improved task completion, and lifted partner product conversion rates.
